newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL SHARES LOWER ON BANK LIQUIDATIONS, WALL ST.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL SHARES LOWER ON BANK LIQUIDATIONS, WALL ST.

text.p: Brazil shares were 2.15 percent lower in thin trade mid-afternoon Monday following a Central Bank decision to close several small financial institutions and losses on Wall Street, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 47 most active stocks was off 261 at 11,868 points at 1515 local/1815 GMT. Total market turnover was much lighter-than-average at 293.3 million reais ($271.5 million).
Traders said the bank liquidations, although expected, contributed to depress prices in a market already speculative ahead of Wednesday's futures index settlement.
Brazil's Central Bank closed down eight small banks and brokerages in connection with a long-running probe into irregular municipal and state debt issues.
"The market would have digested the bank liquidations much easier if it had not been expiration time," one said.
U.S. stock weakness also helped pressuring local share prices as Wall Street remained uneasy about upcoming economic data following steep declines at the end of last week.
Among leading Brazilian shares, benchmark Telebras preferred was off 2.47 percent at 146 reais.
State oil firm Petrobras preferred was down 0.66 percent at 300 reais.
Preferred stock of CVRD, the recently privatized miner, was down 0.04 percent at 27.79 reais, while federal power holding Eletrobras preferred was 1.67 percent lower at 589.99 reais.
